headword: {静脈注射|じょうみゃくちゅうしゃ}
reading: じょうみゃくちゅうしゃ

definitions.explanation: A medical procedure in which medication or fluid is delivered directly into a vein using a needle or catheter. One of the most common medical procedures encountered at hospitals and clinics.

examples.japanese: {静脈注射|じょうみゃくちゅうしゃ}で{薬|くすり}を{投与|とうよ}した。
examples.english: The medication was administered by intravenous injection.

examples.japanese: {脱水症状|だっすいしょうじょう}がひどかったので、{静脈注射|じょうみゃくちゅうしゃ}で{点滴|てんてき}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: The dehydration was severe, so I received an IV drip through an intravenous injection.

examples.japanese: {看護師|かんごし}が{丁寧|ていねい}に{静脈注射|じょうみゃくちゅうしゃ}の{針|はり}を{刺|さ}してくれたので、ほとんど{痛|いた}みを{感|かん}じなかった。
examples.english: The nurse carefully inserted the IV needle, so I hardly felt any pain.

notes:
Composed of {静脈|じょうみゃく} (vein) and {注射|ちゅうしゃ} (injection). Often abbreviated to {静注|じょうちゅう} in medical settings. The English abbreviation IV (intravenous) is also used in Japanese medical contexts.

USAGE:
A practical medical term that anyone visiting a hospital in Japan may encounter. Distinguished from {皮下注射|ひかちゅうしゃ} (subcutaneous injection) and {筋肉注射|きんにくちゅうしゃ} (intramuscular injection) by the route of administration.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {静脈注射|じょうみゃくちゅうしゃ}を{打|う}つ: to give an IV injection
- {静脈注射|じょうみゃくちゅうしゃ}を{受|う}ける: to receive an IV injection
- {静脈注射|じょうみゃくちゅうしゃ}の{針|はり}: IV needle
- {静脈注射|じょうみゃくちゅうしゃ}で{投与|とうよ}する: to administer by IV

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {点滴|てんてき}: IV drip, infusion — continuous slow delivery of fluid into a vein, as opposed to a single injection
- {筋肉注射|きんにくちゅうしゃ}: intramuscular injection — injection into muscle tissue, common for vaccines
- {皮下注射|ひかちゅうしゃ}: subcutaneous injection — injection under the skin, used for insulin and some vaccines
- {注射|ちゅうしゃ}: injection, shot — the general term for any injection
